common_name: Osage orange / Bois d'arc / Bodark / Hedge apple
look_here_first: Start at the TWIG, not the hedge apple: alternate simple glossy smooth-edged leaves, stout single sharp AXILLARY THORNS on many young shoots, and white sticky MILKY LATEX where a twig or leaf is already damaged. Only FEMALE trees may develop the giant knobbly green multiple fruit (which can be seedless without nearby male trees). MALE trees may look fruitless all year.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Deciduous spiny, often low-branching small to medium tree, often formerly planted in hedges; round/irregular crown; trunk with furrowed interlacing bark.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Alternate, simple ovate to elliptic blades, glossy dark green above, 5–13 cm or more, smooth (entire) margins, tapered tips, fine hair mainly beneath in young foliage; deciduous turning yellow in fall. Stipules can be present on young shoots.

key_traits.label: Thorns
key_traits.text: Young fast-growing shoots often have stout rigid axillary thorns near leaf bases. Some older shoots and thornless ornamental forms lack visible thorns; absence alone does not rule it out.

key_traits.label: Latex
key_traits.text: Broken petioles/twigs/fruits can release sticky white milky latex; observe existing damage instead of injuring trees for teaching.

key_traits.label: Flower sex
key_traits.text: Usually dioecious with staminate and pistillate flowers on separate individuals. Staminate flowers in small pendulous greenish spherical/short clustered heads, pistillate flowers in round heads. Individual tiny flowers lack conspicuous petals.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: The huge rough wrinkled yellow-green globose MULTIPLE FRUIT is formed from many flowers crowded in a female head (syncarp of small drupelets), typically about 8–15 cm across. Female trees may produce fruit without a male nearby, but these fruits will lack viable seeds; nearby male pollen is needed for seed set. Male trees do not bear the giant fruits.

key_traits.label: Bark wood
key_traits.text: Mature bark irregular deeply fissured; cut heartwood yellow-orange and prized for durable posts and bow making; wood color in an old cut is not a primary non-destructive field key.
